title: The Last Autopsy
premise: Orsen Galloway, the aging coroner of Hollow Creek, has spent years quietly proving that three 'accidental' deaths were murders — and now someone knows. Twin letters arrive: one confessing to all three killings, one promising a fourth before the statute of limitations expires, each signed with Orsen's own dead wife's initials. As Orsen races to unmask the writer, suspicion falls on everyone who had access to the case files, including the new deputy, Mara Voss, with whom Orsen is falling in love against every instinct of duty and self-preservation. The killer is revealed to be the town's beloved retired judge — the man who sealed the original case files decades ago to protect his own son, whose death Orsen's first 'accident' verdict concealed. In the end, Orsen must choose between arresting the judge and exposing the truth about his own complicity, choosing truth at the cost of the town's forgiveness and nearly his own life.
about_author: Sable Okafor is a former forensic technician turned novelist who grew up in a river town where everyone claimed to know everyone's business and no one knew anything at all. Her fiction explores the quiet rot beneath small-town civility, drawing on her fascination with the people whose job it is to look at the dead.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Orsen Galloway's POV. A slow morning in the morgue establishes Orsen's intimate knowledge of Hollow Creek's dead and his private file of three 'accidents' he quietly proved were murders. Emotional beat: lonely vigilance — a man who trusts the dead more than the living.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Two letters arrive in the same envelope: one confesses to the three deaths in precise detail only the killer could know; the other promises a fourth before the statute expires, signed 'E.G.' — his late wife's initials. Emotional beat: dread and vertigo as his secret work becomes someone else's script.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Reads Autopsies
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. New deputy Mara Voss notices Orsen pulling old case files and confronts him; their friction crackles with mutual recognition — she reads autopsy reports for pleasure too. Emotional beat: wary attraction kindling inside professional suspicion.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He re-examines the third victim, drowned fisherman Dale Pruitt, and finds a ligature mark the original report omitted — meaning someone altered the file after his own examination. Emotional beat: horror that the corruption reaches into his own records.

chapters.title: Sealed by Order
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara discovers all three case files were sealed by judicial order twenty years ago, signed by retired Judge Ambrose Pell. She begins an off-the-books inquiry. Emotional beat: the thrill of a hunt and the first chill of institutional power pushing back.

chapters.title: The Judge's Garden Party
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At a town celebration honoring Judge Pell, Orsen watches the old man charm the crowd and realizes Pell quoted the coroner's report verbatim — details never made public. Emotional beat: polite terror masked by small talk.

chapters.title: A Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A second letter names the fourth victim: 'the one who signed.' Mara and Orsen compare notes for the first time and realize they've been investigating alone in parallel. Emotional beat: alliance forming, intimacy disguised as procedure.

chapters.title: Love Against Protocol
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Working late over the files, Orsen and Mara cross a line neither intended; afterward Orsen pulls away, convinced anyone close to him becomes a target. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into self-protective guilt.

chapters.title: The Son Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Digging into the oldest sealed file, Mara learns Pell's son died twenty-two years ago in an accident Orsen himself ruled accidental — his very first case. Emotional beat: sickening realization that Orsen's career began with a lie.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen confronts his own memory: he falsified his first ruling under pressure from the young deputy DA — Pell himself. The letters aren't from a stranger; they're from someone who watched him do it. Emotional beat: shame surfacing like a body in still water.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara calculates the deadline: eleven days until the fourth murder can be committed without legal consequence. She pushes to go to the state police; Orsen resists, terrified of what exposure means for him. Emotional beat: duty and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Details from their private investigation appear in the county paper, sourced to 'a courthouse official' — someone is watching them and steering the narrative. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a tourniquet.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Signature
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Handwriting analysis suggests the letters were written by two different hands using the same pen — or one hand deliberately split. Mara suspects a second participant. Emotional beat: the case fracturing into mirrors.

chapters.title: Night at the Records Hall
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen breaks into the sealed archives at night and finds the original Pell file mutilated — one page razored out — and fresh boot prints that match the judge's own shoes. Emotional beat: trespasser's adrenaline giving way to certainty.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. reconstructing the missing page from microfilm, Mara finds it was Pell's son's autopsy addendum — evidence the drowning showed defensive wounds. Someone has protected this secret for two decades. Emotional beat: grief for a boy failed by every adult in the room.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen visits Judge Pell under pretense of courtesy; Pell, sharp as ever, implies he knows exactly what Orsen found in the archive and warns him that some truths bury towns. Emotional beat: two men fencing with civility over a shared grave.

chapters.title: The Fourth Letter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A final letter arrives naming the target explicitly: Orsen himself — 'the one who signed,' the last living signature on the false ruling. Deadline: three days. Emotional beat: love and terror fused; Mara refuses to let him face it alone.

chapters.title: Trap at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Orsen and Mara alternate POV. They stage Orsen's 'confession' at the Pruitt boathouse where victim three died, feeding the killer a baited file. Emotional beat: cold courage — turning themselves into the trap.

chapters.title: Who Watches the Watcher
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The trap springs — but not on Pell. It's Pell's protégé, current court clerk Ruth Ann Deverell, who altered the files and wrote the letters to force exposure of the cover-up she helped build. Emotional beat: shock, then pity — a confession born of guilt.

chapters.title: The Judge's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Confronted, Pell admits ordering the cover-up of his son's murder — killed by a business partner the younger Pell was blackmailing — and letting Orsen take the fall unknowingly. He collapses mid-arrest. Emotional beat: power unmasked as nothing but fear in expensive clothes.

chapters.title: Amended Ruling
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen formally amends his first ruling after twenty-two years, reopening all four cases, and testifies against himself for the falsification. Emotional beat: costly absolution — truth purchased with reputation.

chapters.title: Names on Stone
chapters.summary: Orsen and Mara share closing POV. Spring comes; Orsen walks the cemetery renaming graves aloud, now including the judge's son, while Mara waits at the gate — both staying in Hollow Creek, together, having chosen each other over silence. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, love chosen freely after duty is paid.
